candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (422 commits, 5 stars, updated as recently as 2025) with functions to clean and process raw AirDNA property and daily data files, compress/expand STR panels, generate location estimates for listings, identify 'ghost hotel' clusters of private-room listings, flag frequently-rented entire-home properties (i.e. de facto commercial operators), and classify listings against housing-unit inventories. Contains a data-raw folder (likely small reference/test data, not full raw dumps). Requires AirDNA raw files as input, which are paid/licensed, so this is tooling not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs) via a maintained, actively-used methodology for turning AirDNA-style panel data into occupancy/ADR/commercial-operator metrics; also useful for gap #12 (ghost-hotel/illegal-listing detection feeds regulatory-compliance analysis).

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/canada-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: R analysis scripts described as the replication package for Combs, Kerrigan & Wachsmuth 2019 ('Short-Term Rentals in Canada'), a McGill UPGo study of Airbnb activity across major Canadian cities. Repo contains an R/ folder of analysis code; exact data-file contents not confirmed by fetch (GitHub page did not render full README/data listing).
candidates.why_useful: An academic replication package for a peer-reviewed Airbnb-Canada study gives a methodology and possibly underlying panel data for STR supply/pricing in a non-US market not covered by our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/ghost
candidates.what_it_holds: R package/function for identifying 'ghost hotel' clusters (private-room STR listings clustered in a single building/unit acting as an unlicensed hotel), from McGill's UPGo lab.
candidates.why_useful: Methodology for detecting commercial/illegal STR operators, relevant to gap #12 (regulatory/registration compliance) and to separating true P2P supply from de facto hotel supply within STR panels.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/raffle
candidates.what_it_holds: R package implementing a function for probabilistically assigning STR listings to administrative geographies (e.g. census tracts/neighbourhoods) when only approximate listing coordinates are known.
candidates.why_useful: Method for geocoding fuzzy STR listing locations into standard geographies, useful for building regional (city/neighbourhood-level) STR supply panels from Inside-Airbnb-style data with imprecise coordinates.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/toronto-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill UPGo lab's analysis of Toronto's STR market (city-specific study, MIT licensed); likely built on AirDNA-derived panel data for Toronto pre-dating our current 13-city Inside Airbnb coverage.
candidates.why_useful: City-specific STR supply/activity study for a market (Toronto) not in our current Inside Airbnb panel; could extend geographic coverage or provide a cross-check methodology.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/vancouver-regulations
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed McGill UPGo analysis of STR host compliance with Vancouver's 2018 short-term-rental regulations (registration/licensing compliance study).
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-point for gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration trackers) for Vancouver, one of the cities named in that gap list.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/halifax-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill UPGo STR market report/analysis for Halifax, Nova Scotia (2 stars, updated as recently as 2025 per org metadata).
candidates.why_useful: Smaller secondary Canadian market STR study; fills out a broader Canadian STR supply picture beyond Toronto/Montreal.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/whitehorse-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed McGill UPGo report on STR activity in Whitehorse, Yukon.
candidates.why_useful: Niche small-market STR study; low direct relevance to ABNB's financial KPIs but a genuine data/analysis artifact.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/caribbean-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed McGill UPGo analysis prepared for a presentation on Caribbean STR markets.
candidates.why_useful: Touches gap #7-adjacent territory (regional travel/STR volume outside the US/EU core), Caribbean STR supply not covered elsewhere in our holdings.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/florida-presentation
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill UPGo presentation materials/analysis prepared for a Florida Realtors conference, on STR market activity in Florida.
candidates.why_useful: Florida STR supply/pricing angle; could complement Hawaii DBEDT as a state-level STR/tourism data point (gap #8 state-level occupancy mentions Florida bed tax).

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/Starkville_analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill UPGo analysis of STR activity in the US South, focused on Starkville, MS and similar smaller cities.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — a small-market case study; listed for completeness of the UPGo body of work.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/charlottetown-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill UPGo STR market analysis for Charlottetown, PEI.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal small-market Canadian STR case study.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/la-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill UPGo STR analysis of the Los Angeles market (2019).
candidates.why_useful: LA is already in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; this could be a cross-check dataset/methodology or an earlier vintage (2019) than our current holdings.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps geography with our existing LA Inside Airbnb coverage but from a different (AirDNA-derived) source and earlier vintage.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/upgo
candidates.what_it_holds: General 'UPGo utility package' (R, 217 commits) underlying the lab's other STR analysis repos — shared helper functions for their data pipeline.
candidates.why_useful: Supporting library for the strr/ghost/raffle ecosystem; only useful in combination with those.

candidates.name: CodeForBc/airbnb-regulation
candidates.what_it_holds: Civic-tech (Code for BC) project with 269 commits, MIT licensed, that scrapes Airbnb listings and cross-references them against BC business-registry records to flag STR listings operating in violation of BC's short-term-rental registration policy; includes Docker/Terraform infra and a Grafana dashboard for results.
candidates.why_useful: A working method for turning STR registration/compliance policy into a quantifiable violation rate, relevant to gap #12 (city/provincial STR registration datasets). Note: it scrapes airbnb.com directly, so per repo rules this is catalogued as a method only and must not be run without a human ToS decision.

candidates.name: urban-displacement/displacement-typologies
candidates.what_it_holds: UC Berkeley Urban Displacement Project repo (GPL-3.0, 502 commits, updated Aug 2026, 49 stars) with GeoPackage/CSV files and a codebook classifying census tracts in 8 US metros (Atlanta, Bay Area, Chicago, Cleveland, Denver, LA, Memphis, Seattle) into 8 gentrification/displacement typology categories, mostly on 2017-2018 vintage census/demographic data. Confirmed by fetch: no Airbnb/STR variables included.
candidates.why_useful: Relevant to gap #13 (long-term rental/housing economics, host-supply pressure) as a housing-displacement/gentrification classification that could be joined to STR listing density by tract to study host-supply drivers, though it carries no STR data itself.

candidates.name: RomanKhazin/Toronto-Short-Term-Rentals
candidates.what_it_holds: Small individual repo (2021) with a single Jupyter notebook exploring the City of Toronto's public short-term-rental registration open dataset; no committed raw data files were visible in the repo listing (notebook likely pulls from Toronto Open Data directly).
candidates.why_useful: Points to Toronto's official STR registration open-data feed (a municipal registry, gap #12) via a working notebook, though the notebook itself adds little beyond exploration.

notes: WebSearch's session budget (shared across all scouts) was already exhausted (200/200) before any query in this theme ran, so no WebSearch results were obtained at all. DuckDuckGo HTML search returned only a CAPTCHA challenge page for every query. Bing search (via WebFetch) loaded but returned results completely unrelated to the query terms (YouTube/OBS/TikTok pages) for both queries tried, suggesting Bing's non-JS results page is not usable this way in this session. All real findings in this run came from `gh search repos` and `gh api`, which worked but hit GitHub's secondary rate limit twice (403) requiring a short backoff; a couple of planned follow-up searches (wachsmuth airbnb, university replication) were lost to the second rate-limit hit and not retried further given the ~25-tool-call budget. The one clear win: McGill's UPGo lab (Urban Politics and Governance, David Wachsmuth) publishes its entire STR-research toolkit and most city case studies as a GitHub org (UPGo-McGill, 29 repos) — this is exactly the 'McGill UPGo' target named in the theme and had not obviously been catalogued yet. Its core packages (strr, ghost, raffle) are AirDNA-data-cleaning/commercial-operator-detection tools rather than committed datasets (AirDNA itself is paid), so treat them as methodology to fill gap #2, not as a data source in hand. Did not find a McGill/UPGo-style lab with committed *raw* historical Inside Airbnb mirrors (gap #1) in this pass — worth a dedicated follow-up scout specifically hunting Inside-Airbnb pre-2023 archive mirrors and NYC 2023-06→2024-03 gap-fillers, ideally once WebSearch budget resets, since gh search's free-text matching on GitHub's descriptions/README is comparatively weak for that kind of query.
